correctness.rationale: For commutative unital Artinian A, write A=∏ A_i local. In a local factor all nonzero ideals contain a simple ideal in the socle S. If C is not simple, choosing a simple L and J=mC gives C⊆(J:ann L)=[L:J] although C is in neither L nor mC (Nakayama), hence not coprime. If socle dimension>1, each simple C is similarly excluded with another simple L and J=0. If socle dimension=1, unique simple S is essential in every nonzero ideal and is coprime. In products, a two-coordinate supported ideal C decomposes I+J and violates coprimality since C ann(I) ⊆J; one-coordinate coprime property reduces to the local factor. Thus exactly one coprime ideal per Gorenstein local component, and its annihilator is the corresponding maximal ideal. All subsets arise as V_c(I) so topology is finite discrete. Independently enumerated all six ideals of F2[x,y]/(x,y)^2 using explicit F2^3 multiplication and verified no coprime ideals. This is corroboration of the full proof, not its substitute.

originality.rationale: Murphy-Hernandez and Leon-Rodriguez 2026 define the coproduct and coprime spectrum and prove equivalence with ordinary prime spectrum for dual rings, with a non-Gorenstein square-zero local example. The present classification covers every commutative Artinian ring, including non-dual local factors and arbitrary mixed products, and identifies the exact Gorenstein local locus. The classical zero-dimensional Gorenstein socle criterion is used, not claimed novel. No matching classification found in Resultary semantics or prior ring-spectrum articles searched, but earlier lattice terminology remains a risk.
